sources.citation: Chirimaunga, Tendai & Nhira Edgar Mberi. 2026. Linguistic fieldwork: The case of Chibarwe orthography in Zimbabwe. Drumspeak: International Journal of Research in the Humanities 7(2): 106-131. DOI 10.47963/drumspeak.v7i2.2210
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Read in full (23 pp.): orthography-design methodology; mentions that elders insisted on representing vowel-length contrasts (p. 119 of the text, line 442 of the extract) and that songs were recorded 'to capture prosodic patterns'; no statement on stress or tone. Reference list cites Mangoya & Ngunga 2013 (the UEM doctoral dissertation), Hachipola 1998, Doke 1931, Chirimaunga 2025 (causatives in ChiBarwe, JLLE 19(1)).

Revista Científica da Universidade Eduardo Mondlane, Série: Letras e Ciências Sociais 5(2): 35-42. DOI 10.70778/14cqv861 (text in English, abstract in Portuguese)

sources.note: Nothing. Read in full (8 pp.): morphophonology of class 9/10 nasal prefixes and CV syllable structure only; the words stress, accent, tone, pitch, prosody do not occur. Cites Mangoya 2013 (UEM PhD thesis) as the source on Barwe phonology.

sources.citation: Mangoya, Esau & Gift Mheta. 2016. A comparative study of operations of liquids in Barwe and Central Shona. Language Matters 47(2): 151-165. DOI 10.1080/10228195.2016.1179779 (green OA copy, DUT OpenScholar, via Unpaywall)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Read in full: distribution of /l/, [ɾ], [r] in Barwe vs Zezuru/Karanga; no statement on stress, accent or tone. Calls Barwe 'a variety of Eastern Shona' (following Alfandega et al. 2008) and cites Mangoya 2013, Segmental phonology of Barwe with some articulatory phonetics, Maputo: Ciedima Lda (book form of the thesis).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Sena language' (Barwe language redirects there); Glottolog languoid page barw1243 (classification Senaic > Sena-Nyanja > Tumbuka-Sena-Nyanja)
sources.note: No stress statement for Barwe. Wikipedia treats Rue/Barwe/Cibalke as a divergent dialect of Sena; Glottolog keeps Barwe as a separate Senaic language, while Mangoya & Mheta 2016 call it Eastern Shona.

sources.note: Each language chapter of the NELIMO/CEA orthography reports gives a phoneme inventory, syllable structure and a note on tone/prosody for orthographic purposes; the Cibalke chapter is the standard Mozambican reference for the language and may state penultimate prominence or tone.

sources.note: Recent Zimbabwean primary work on ChiBarwe by a fieldworker; the background section may summarise ChiBarwe phonology including prosody. Low likelihood of a stress statement.

sources.citation: Mangoya, Esau. 2012/2013. Segmental phonology of Barwe with some articulatory phonetics. PhD dissertation, Universidade Eduardo Mondlane, Maputo (276 pp.); published Maputo: Ciedima Lda, 2013.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only full phonology of Barwe (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a phonology; author's own later papers cite it as the source on Barwe sounds). A 276-page phonology thesis normally has a suprasegmental section covering tone, vowel length and stress/penultimate lengthening; this is the work most likely to hold the deciding statement.

sources.citation: Alfandega, P., A. Chebanne, W. Chigidi, H. Chimhundu et al. 2008. A unified standard orthography for Shona-Nyai language varieties: Botswana, Mozambique and Zimbabwe. Cape Town: CASAS.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: CASAS harmonised-orthography monograph that explicitly includes Barwe in the Shona-Nyai cluster; such monographs carry short phonology tables and prosodic notes (tone, length) for the member varieties.

sources.citation: Hachipola, Simooya Jerome. 1998. A survey of the minority languages of Zimbabwe. Harare: University of Zimbabwe Publications.

sources.note: Only survey covering Zimbabwean Barwe (Tonga of Mudzi = Barwe per Glottolog); sociolinguistic, so unlikely to state stress, but it is the work Glottolog uses for subclassification comments.

PhD dissertation, Universidade Eduardo Mondlane, Maputo, 276 pp; published Maputo: Ciedima Lda, 2013 (Glottolog ref 317858, listed by Glottolog as a phonology; cited by Mangoya & Mheta 2016, Mangoya 2025, Chirimaunga & Mberi 2026)
sources.note: Unknown. The earlier scan mislabelled it a University of Zimbabwe thesis; every record seen today (Glottolog, the author's own citations, the Drumspeak reference list naming Ngunga as co-author/supervisor) gives Universidade Eduardo Mondlane. www.repositorio.uem.mz (196.3.97.27) and ir.uz.ac.zw (196.4.80.201) both refuse connections; the the Internet Archive has no capture of either search page. Glottolog's hh archive holds a PDF (bestfn africa\), so a digital copy exists.
